brief: Goldman recommends a barbell of selective AI exposure plus defensive, high-FCF names, after a post-midterm relief rally lasted under a day and AI/geopolitics fatigue resumed. Last week's washout sparked a rebound attempt, but appetite to digest NVDA-specific issues faded fast and desk conversations called it a bear-market rally. Whether the selloff is a buyable dip or a leadership regime shift hinges on whether AI is an earnings bubble. Valuations in some pockets price excessive downward revisions to 2027 earnings, so renewed AI confidence could double memory stocks. Goldman likes adding longs in its SPXXAI basket. Mega-cap index weights now lack free cash flow, so Goldman expects FCF generators to keep outperforming and prefers long-FCF over low-FCF names, short its Lending Sensitive basket. The European FCF pair is catching up after lagging over summer. China's high-dividend/SOE trade, helped by National Team buying and heavy buybacks/dividends, has beaten the CSI 300 by 23 points over three months. Europe's low AI beta argues for diversification via its breaking-out High/Stable Margins basket, though French Domestics' 10% rally should reverse given credit conditions before S&P's Nov 27 review. Cross-horizon momentum correlations have turned negative as AI positioning unwinds, with elevated volatility signaling more rotations ahead.
